# the contributor audit: body-tied buffer and coherent projective charts

Sources read in full:

- `candidate 26455afca6af9c16`
- `candidate f29d64ab4f68c3cc`
- `candidate 2a206064c18d19c5`


transfer, and response computations PASS under their explicitly named
archived compact-class and ordinary energy inputs. The new H separator
remains conditional in the version audited here; its actual construction
has been separately requested. This audit is not a numerical OC payment.

## 1. The profile and normalization

Set N=d+1, F=E^(1/d), v=V^(1/d), H=F^(d/N)v^(1/N).
The increasing concave weighted geometric mean preserves their joint
concavity. Since grad_x log E=N a at the attained ordinary projective
normalizer, grad_x log H=a exactly. The dimensionless buffer must be
f_H=H/M^(1/d). It satisfies f_H<=(V/M)^(1/d)<=1.
Substitution into (L E/M)^(1/N) gives L=(V/M)^(1/d);
omitting the M in this tied multiplier would change the response.

## 2. Source faces and global chart supports

At an integer relative-interior source-face witness, a strictly positive
anchored representation and the exact energy equality theorem give
pointed homothety. Perturbing the same positive representation by both
signs of every affine dependence gives affine center and scale maps.
For any continuous support normal, the finite support-LP majorant at
that witness agrees at every source in the face. It therefore agrees
on the entire real face. This proves actual real-fiber homothety,
including possible contributions from fibers outside the face.

The positive base-affine scale extension follows from a finite
supergradient of the concave volume-root profile. The finite-hull
support LP provides a uniform Hausdorff-Lipschitz bound, and the
uniform positive inradius gives the required volume-root Lipschitz
bound, even at a boundary base. The infimal-convolution extension of
the negative profile then supplies a finite subgradient there.

If S>=F and T>=v are affine supports at a mark, its normalized chart is
R=(d/N)S/F_Y+(1/N)T/v_Y. On the own fiber it equals
1+a_Y.(X-y). Globally R>=v_min/(N v_Y)>0. In particular its ordinary
own-fiber denominator is >=1/N. These statements require neither the
old free multiplier nor its parameter martingale.

The cross-source chart comparison and scaling are exact weighted
AM--GM. After scaling by b_i=(F_i/L_i)^(d/N)(v_i/L_i)^(1/N),
the lower envelope U of the charts majorizes H and touches every
original source. All comparison cycles have product at least one.
The recorded entropy decomposition follows by integrating the exact
row mass-one chart ratios. Each term is nonnegative, but parameter
stationarity does not force the sum to vanish.

## 3. Compactness and the direct buffer gap

The cited compact positive minimal-bad class is an input, not reproved
here. Within it, uniform markwise cap continuity follows from the
all-orientation slab estimate after dividing by the continuous-normal
length. Base tilt therefore does not spoil uniformity. Pure-base caps
use only finitely many fiber subsets. Energy continuity, covariance
continuity and the bound f_H<=1 supply fixed-epsilon attainment.

Every ordinary maximum has depth at least Gamma_d/|P|. The own-mark
Lipschitz bound and zero depth at an own boundary point put each such
maximum in a uniform own-fiber core. An ambient supporting cap at the
boundary is supplied by the finite support LP with nonzero continuous
normal; its mixed d-volume is zero.

At these marks, energy monotonicity bounds E below by the centered
inball volume. Every nonvertical cap gains a uniform own-ball strip
of order epsilon. Pure-base caps have the exact reserve V_p/2.
Thus the stated two-sided linear value gap is uniform. The same
markwise upper estimate puts buffered maxima in a uniform core and
makes all their deepest groups proper for small epsilon. The optional
epsilon~tau scale selection has the same compact scalar proof as the
archived logarithmic penalty, without any free-parameter limit.

## 4. Response constants and scope

For inward rates D_p, total D, and energy rate C_E,

    dot(log f_H)=-C_E/(N E)-D_p/(d N V_p)+D/(d M).

The pooled covariance norm contributes D/(2M)-J/(2M), so the positive
global D coefficient in the full buffer derivative is

    1/(d M)+1/(2M)=(d+2)/(2d M).

Reversing the buffer term in the contact budget gives the recorded
positive energy, own-volume and covariance densities, and the negative
global coefficient. Hence, IF the new actual common separator is
constructed, its surface source A is positive and is dominated in
conditional convex order by

    [beta+(d+2)Delta/(2d M)] dS.

The source is a measure on actual boundary points, not on deepest
marks. Affine tests give conditional masses and full first moments;
they do not create the old volume-row certificate. Uniform denominator,
energy, volume and coarea bounds exclude inverse-parameter concentration
within this response. Supporting-cap allocations remain necessary.

The separately requested next obligation is to construct this new
finite cover and simultaneous physical response cone, and then the
actual separator, without inheriting a certificate from the different
free-parameter problem. No outside-contact or Gamma payment follows
from the response identity alone.
